posts.name: eggroll20xd6
posts.cooked:
Maynes32:

 

Spiff wrote:
 Powerhound_2000 wrote:
That has been the case for the entire game why change now?   
Because the game is done!The fact that everyone here has their own theories about what's going on in that pit tells me that we don't actually have the real story.  I have to admit that if I'm expected to buy the RPG to get the story for the game I've been paying for for 5 years, I may just say forget it.Yes, I'm in a mood today.
I had a long rant about this. Instead I'm just going to agree ;)

 

Here is what I think about the whole "story" of Sentinels of the Multiverse.  Christopher has given us a world and he hasn't given us much detail because of the title of the game itself.  The multiverse is us and while we have comic numbers listed on each card and we have no idea where they really fit in terms of an official GTG storyline, if all we wanted was that story, I'm sure it will be given to us eventually.  I think its fun to think that maybe we encounter some heroes that we see in the early boxes later, but they foreshadow what is to come.

Take the Visionary for example, if we were to look at a chronological timeline of the comic history, in my opinion, she would show up closer to the Shattered Timelines part of the story instead of near the beginning of Sentinel Comics due to her whole time travel thing.  However, others could see her coming in sooner, but even though we don't know when she actually shows up, we still include her in our fights against Baron Blade, Voss, Omnitron, and Dawn.  It would kind of suck to just have a character sitting in a box for story purposes, especially if that character is one of your favorites.  Heck, AZ doesn't appear until FFA#5 (I think, don't have the cards in my had atm).  

For me personally, I've been trying to figure out where characters and things take place from the cards for a long time mainly for fan fiction purposes, but you know what, that's the fun of having this multiverse, it is what you create.  Look at Razor's Edge, it's an awesome story, and it got placed in the SotM:VG.  Does it need more context than what it gave? Maybe, but is it any less good? Nope. I continue to write from time to time and even hope to put it in the fan fiction section again (it's been a while).  Whether people read it or not, it's the story I want to tell and ultimately people can enjoy that or not. Even in comics today with everything rebooting, they are starting with characters and a blank canvas essentially.  Where those writers/creators go with those stories is up to them, just as much as this story is up to us.

On that note, I would love to see the GTG storyline timeline just so I can see what Christopher and Adam had intended from their perspective.

posts.cooked:
I'm in the same boat, Eggroll - the continuity of my own games has long since diverged from canon.  I don't feel constrained by anything canonical (down to my Wraith and AZ getting totally different origins), so I'm not as upset as many people seem to by limited information - but I'll admit I do find it an odd choice.Why not provide more details?  It's not like novel or television writers refusing to give spoilers, because the plot is not the main product they're selling, and could be a promotion.  Still, we get enough details to be helpful fodder for my group's concepts, so I can't complain.

 

(The Visionary was totally there when Blade brought down the moon, though - it's in her flavor text!)
